The Democratic tsunami isn't just washing away living fossils like Susan
Collins, but U.S. military contractor profits as well.

Shares plummeted today as investors anticipated a retreat from the Iran war.
(This despite the fact that the DOW shot up by about 3 percent today -- its
best day since April.)

Meanwhile, Vice President JD Vance issued an extraordinary
[statement](https://x.com/JDVance/status/2118004988433641835) on X (nee
Twitter) blaming his party's wipeout at the midterms on the Iran War.

"The reason we lost is the war," he said.

If only there were a position in the White House that couldn't be fired, let's
say a "Vice President," who could've prevented the war … Oh well!

Be on the lookout in the coming days as the bullshit machine seeds anonymously
sourced claims that Vance was privately against the war all along.

Most interesting in Vance's statement was a hint at concession to the
Democrats.

"I'm open to the idea that we should change [immigration] enforcement--by
focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance," Vance
said.

Donald Trump said much the same in an interview with Politico late last night.

Trump said:

> "Well, we're going to work with the Democrats to make sure things go well
> for our country. Very important. They've already called and they want to
> work with me."

So you can expect the Trump-Mamdani bromance to expand and maybe even produce
some concessions.

At the top of the concessions list will be Iran.

So not only is there not going to be a nuclear strike on Iran -- a fiction
propagated by Tucker Carlson this week (which Trump actually dismissed in the
Politico interview) -- but as I reported on Monday, it's unlikely there will
be any major strikes on Iran now.

"We seem to be getting everything we want," Trump told _Financial Times_ last
night. "We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason
for it."

Asked when the Iran war will end, Trump this morning said, "Whenever I want it
to."

That does not mean it will be easy for Trump to extract himself before a
Democratic Congress is seated in January.

Just yesterday, Iranian armed forces chief of staff Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi
laid out five conditions for Iran:

  1. Ending fighting on "all fronts," including Lebanon and Gaza; 

  2. Lift sanctions and frozen Iranian funds; 

  3. Pay reparations; 

  4. Recognize Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz; 

  5. Provide security guarantees against future attacks. 

There is an immediate and possible negotiating package that Iran offered on
Monday, but it represents a hardliner position that is a nonstarter for
Washington. The U.S. "diplomatic" position is that Iran must give up its
nuclear aspirations and capabilities first, something that Trump doesn't
really care about.

What he does care about is money and business, so some combination of ending
the naval blockade, cancelling sanctions, freeing up money for Iran, and
allowing Iranian oil sales to resume is most likely on the president's mind.

And then there's actually ending the Iran war, as in ceasing to see the
Islamic Republic as an enemy of the United States and reversing 47 years of
being stuck as the American Satan. But endless war never quite ends, that's
why it's called endless war.

Remember that only Joe Biden actually "ended" a Middle East war, in
Afghanistan. Except that it is now another character in the endless war game.
Obama may have pretended to end the Iraq fighting, but some American forces
stayed in Iraq and they built up in Syria to fight ISIS. In his second term,
Donald Trump does seem to have to have withdrawn those forces, closing the
largest U.S. base in Iraq at Erbil and closing the Syrian bases at Qasrak and
al-Tanf.

That is, if American forces actually withdrew. If experience is any guide,
U.S. fighting just continues if only in more secret form. Now, instead of
"boots," there's covert operations, special operations, normal operations
taking place in the shadows, and even loafers on the ground (that's the very
definition of "endless" war).

And for every Afghanistan or Iraq or Syria, something takes its place: there's
been a massive buildup in Jordan, forces stay in Kuwait, and there's a new and
growing American presence in Israel. "Over-the-horizon" operations against al
Qaeda and the Taliban in Afghanistan continue from Qatar, Pakistan,
Uzbekistan, and the other Stans. There is never a real end, and certainly the
military is not bugging out because it can say that it is leaving Democracies
behind, or even stability.

But who knows? Maybe someday there will be a Trump hotel in Tehran.
